text:
The biggest story in Detroit this season ended on Nov. 22, when the Red Wings traded their captain, Dylan Larkin, to Montreal. Larkin had asked out and refused to play until he was moved, and the saga got ugly enough that, per a Daily Faceoff report, police were guarding his home after the request. The return centered on Kirby Dach and prospect Michael Hage, plus draft capital.

The hockey has been grim through all of it. Detroit is 9-12-3 with 21 points and 3-7-0 in its last 10. The chances are close to even, 49% of the expected goals at 5v5, but the Red Wings have scored about 10 fewer goals than those chances deserved. Alex DeBrincat has two points in his last 10 games against 8.3 our numbers expected; that drought is due to end. Lucas Raymond, who scored the lone goal in Wednesday's loss to Boston, has said plainly that Detroit has to find more offense.

There are things to like. Daniil Tarasov is at .933 over his last five starts, saving 5.1 goals above expected, even with a 2-3-0 record. The young line of DeBrincat, Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard has 63% of the expected goals and has outscored teams 8-1. Marco Kasper is back and Todd McLellan is weighing a bigger role for him.

Our simulations give Detroit a 13% playoff chance. What to watch: where Dach fits, and how fast.
headline: After Larkin, the Red Wings start over
